categories.name: regulation
categories.definition: A binding legal or regulatory requirement that constrains who may operate, where, when, or how. Typically uses obligation language (must, may not, no person may), cites a code section (e.g., § 107.x), and is enforceable by a regulatory body. Distinguish from safety_constraint (a configurable software/operational rule) and procedure (a sequence of actions).
exemplars: The groundspeed of the small unmanned aircraft may not exceed 87 knots (100 miles per hour).
No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft over a human being unless that human being is directly participating in the operation of the small unmanned aircraft.
The minimum distance of the small unmanned aircraft from clouds must be no less than 500 feet below the cloud and 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud.
After May 17, 2021, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system at night under a certificate of waiver issued prior to April 21, 2021 under § 107.200 of this part.
boundary_cases: If the chunk states a constraint but is from a software/configuration manual rather than a legal code, prefer safety_constraint.
If the chunk lists altitude/speed as a product capability rather than a permitted limit, prefer specification.

categories.name: definition
categories.definition: A terminological definition that introduces a term and gives its meaning. Often follows the form 'X means Y' or 'X: <definition>'. Single-clause and self-contained. Distinguish from principle (explanatory prose about how something works).
exemplars: Control station: An interface used by the remote pilot to control the flight path of the small unmanned aircraft.
Small unmanned aircraft: An unmanned aircraft weighing less than 55 pounds on takeoff, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft.

Visual observer: A person who is designated by the remote pilot in command to assist the remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls of the small UAS to see and avoid other air traffic or objects aloft or on the ground.
A quadcopter is a type of helicopter or multicopter that has four rotors.
boundary_cases: If the chunk defines a term but also imposes an obligation in the same sentence, label as both definition and regulation (multi-label).
If the chunk explains how a defined thing works rather than naming it, prefer principle.

categories.name: specification
categories.definition: A quantitative or model-specific component fact: a part number, a numeric capability, a material, a sensor model, a battery capacity, a frequency band. Typically reads like a row in a bill of materials or a spec sheet. Distinguish from regulation (which constrains use rather than describing a product).
exemplars: Battery: 5870 mAh
Camera: Sony Exmor 1/2.3", 4K at 30 FPS
Transmission: Lightbridge (5 km range)
Propellers: Model 9450S
GNSS: Real-time kinematic module; compatible with GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou
boundary_cases: If the spec appears inside a procedure step (e.g., 'connect the 5V rail'), prefer procedure unless the line is purely descriptive.
If a number expresses an operational ceiling rather than a product trait, prefer regulation or safety_constraint.

categories.name: procedure
categories.definition: An imperative, ordered, or step-wise instruction that the reader is meant to perform: 'connect X to Y', 'mount the GPS', 'flash the firmware', 'calibrate the compass'. Action-oriented. Distinguish from regulation (an external constraint) and specification (a static fact).
exemplars: Connect the GPS to the TELEM2 port on the flight controller.
Mount the flight controller on the frame using vibration-damping standoffs.
Power the system from a bench supply before connecting the battery for the first time.
Bind the receiver to the transmitter following the manufacturer's pairing sequence.
Calibrate the compass by rotating the airframe through each axis as prompted by the ground station.
boundary_cases: If the chunk gives a numbered list of legal requirements (do X, do Y), prefer regulation — the imperative form alone isn't enough.
If the step is conditional on a failure ('if the battery falls below 20%, return to home'), prefer safety_constraint.

categories.name: principle
categories.definition: Explanatory prose describing how or why something works: physical principles, design rationale, historical context, comparative analysis. Not a definition (no 'X means Y' form), not a step, not a constraint, not a part. Distinguish from definition (which names a term) by length and discursive style.
exemplars: Quadcopters typically have two rotors spinning clockwise and two counterclockwise. Flight control works through independent speed variation of each rotor.
When all four rotors spin at equal angular velocity with opposing directions, the net torque cancels out. This eliminates the need for a tail rotor found on conventional helicopters.
The quadcopter configuration gained popularity with advances in electronics around 2005–2010.
The small size and low inertia of modern drones make them practical for flight control systems that would be impractical for larger aircraft.
boundary_cases: If the prose is followed by an action the reader must take, split the chunk and label the imperative half as procedure.
Marketing copy and historical anecdotes both fall here unless they introduce a defined term.

categories.name: safety_constraint
categories.definition: A configurable failsafe, threshold, or automated protective response inside a software/operational system: battery thresholds, geofence limits, RC-loss responses, kill switches, flight termination. Typically tied to a specific autopilot or vehicle configuration rather than to a legal authority. Distinguish from regulation (external/legal) and procedure (manual action).
exemplars: Failsafes allow you to specify areas and conditions under which you can safely fly, and the action that will be performed if a failsafe is triggered.
Battery Management: Three-tier system with warning, critical, and emergency thresholds triggering progressively severe responses.
Kill Switch: Stops motors instantly (reversible within timeout period).
Geofence: Breach of cylindrical perimeter triggers specified actions based on horizontal radius and altitude limits.
Data Link Loss: Engages when telemetry connection to ground control is severed.
boundary_cases: If a constraint is expressed as a legal obligation (no person may, must), prefer regulation even if it concerns safety.
If the chunk is just describing what a switch is rather than what it triggers, prefer specification.
